title: Immunofluorescence on FFPE Tissue Sections from Human Gut
author: Ross J Porter
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bsqendte
materials: Make sodium citrate retrieval buffer as below (adapted from Abcam ) : Dissolve 2.94 g tri-sodium citrate (dihydrate) in 1 L dH2O Titrate to pH 6.4 using 1N hydrochloric acid Add 0.5 µL Tween®20 (Sigma-Aldrich, 9005-64-5) For our experiments, HIER buffer was made fresh each time (as 0.5-1L total was needed). However, Abcam suggest buffer is stable for 3 months at room temperature, or longer at 4 º C.

Dilute the primary antibody/antibodies in 10% donkey serum diluted in 1x PBS - make enough for 300 µL, per slide . DO NOT USE ANY DETERGENTS (e.g. Tween ® ), as this will remove TrueBlack ® from the tissue. Example: Mouse monoclonal anti-human CD3 antibody (ab699 [GR3295418-1]) at 1:50

Dilute the secondary antibody/antibodies in 10% donkey serum diluted in PBS - make enough for 300 µL, per slide . Example: Donkey anti-mouse ab150108 at 1:500 (Alexa Fluor ® 594 ) DO NOT USE ANY DETERGENTS (e.g. Tween ® ), as this will remove TrueBlack ® .

Analyse objectively with a digital image-analysis software. QuPath (an open-source software) analysis works well for this application in our laboratory. Ensure you use the negative control to 'gate' out residual background staining/ autofluorescence. QuPath: Open source software for digital pathology image analysis.. Scientific reports.

This protocol has been optimised using reagents in our laboratory to stain full thickness FFPE biopsies from inflamed and non-inflamed human gut specimens. We encourage further optimisation experiments in other laboratories, with different tissue sections and antibodies. Specific optimisation suggestions are listed below: Check there is no inadvertent damage occurring to tissue sections Ensure slides are not drying out, especially during antigen-retrieval in the microwave or during antibody incubation Ensure all timings and temperatures are accurate, especially during antigen retrieval Beware of chemical reagents that make tissue distortion or damage more likely (e.g. EDTA, Tween) Issues with antibody-epitope binding Alter deparaffinisation and rehydration times Increase or decrease heat-induced epitope retrieval (HIER) time Trial higher temperatures for HIER; consider use of a pressure cooker or autoclave Use a more accurate time and temperature controlled microwave (professional rather than household) Trial different reagents for HIER e.g. Tris-EDTA Trial different pH levels for HIER buffers Reduce the time of primary antibody application (e.g. from overnight to 1 hour) Increase or decrease concentration of Tween (beware of increased tissue distortion at higher concentrations) Increase or decrease antibody concentrations (primary and secondary) If necessary, consider different fixation methods for your tissue To optimise fluorescence and reduce autofluorescence/ non-specific background staining Ensure you have robust positive and negative controls for every experiment Increase the blocking time Increase the number and duration of washing steps Protect slides from light during staining and imaging Attempt multiple staining steps (i.e. stain for each antibody sequentially) Alter the time slides are exposed to TrueBlack® (e.g. decrease to 15s or increase to 1 minute) If there are issues with both antigen retrieval and fluorescence, try applying TrueBlack® at the end of this protocol before mounting (this will also allow increased use of detergents before this step) - see data sheet for TrueBlack ® . If TrueBlack® is not effective for your tissues, consider other agents such as Vector®TrueVIEW® Autofluorescence Quenching Kit (SP-8400-15). Ensure the cover slip and mounting medium are optimal for your detection (and compatible with immunofluorescence) Ensure the best fluorophores are selected for imaging, and ensure there is good separation between fluorophores for co-stains Ensure there are no dust or bubbles on the side at time of mounting If the final staining results are inconsistent, consider use of an autostainer or optimising slide scanner settings.

Analyse objectively with a digital image-analysis software. QuPath (an open-source software) analysis works well for this application in our laboratory. Ensure you use the negative control to 'gate' out residual background staining/ autofluorescence. QuPath: Open source software for digital pathology image analysis.. Scientific reports.

steps.title: Deparaffinize and rehydrate slides
steps.instruction: Sequentially immerse slides in a slide rack into the following solutions for the indicated times:

steps.title: Rinse in tap water
steps.instruction: Place the slides immediately into tap water to prevent tissue dehydration; never allow the tissue to become dehydrated.

steps.title: Preheat retrieval buffer
steps.instruction: Heat the retrieval buffer in a thermosetting plastic container in a microwave at 800 W full power for 3 min or until boiling/bubbling.

steps.title: Perform heat‑induced epitope retrieval
steps.instruction: Immerse slides (in a slide rack) in the pre‑heated retrieval buffer and microwave on full power for 20 min. Add extra retrieval buffer at 7 min and again at 14 min to keep slides fully immersed.

steps.title: Cool slides in cold water
steps.instruction: Cool the slides in cold running tap water.

steps.title: Permeabilize with Triton X‑100
steps.instruction: Immerse slides in 0.1 % Triton X‑100 (dissolved in PBS) for 15 min.

steps.title: Wash slides with PBS
steps.instruction: Wash the slides with PBS for the indicated times.

steps.title: Prepare TrueBlack quencher
steps.instruction: Make TrueBlack® Lipofuscin Autofluorescence Quencher 20X (Cat 23007, Biotium) for 250 µL per slide (1 : 20 dilution).

substeps.instruction: Vortex the stock TrueBlack® for 5 s.
Vortex the diluted solution for 5 s.

steps.title: Apply TrueBlack quencher
steps.instruction: Lay slides horizontally in a humidity/moisture chamber, wipe away excess PBS with soft tissue (do not dry), then apply 250 µL of the diluted TrueBlack® solution to each slide for 30 s. Process only 2–3 slides at a time using a stopwatch. Do not use any detergents thereafter.

steps.title: Prepare blocking solution
steps.instruction: Prepare blocking solution in PBS containing 25 % donkey serum and 10 % fetal calf serum; make 300 µL per slide.

steps.title: Wash before blocking
steps.instruction: Rinse slides with PBS for 2 s, then perform three PBS washes of 5 min each.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Apply 300 µL blocking solution to each slide, gently cover the whole slide with cut‑to‑shape Parafilm®M, lay slides horizontally in a humidity chamber, tip off excess block, and incubate in a closed humidity/moisture chamber at room temperature for 1 h.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Apply 300 µL primary antibody solution to each slide, cover with Parafilm®M, and place in a closed humidity/moisture chamber at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Wash after primary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash slides with PBS three times, 5 min each.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Lay slides horizontally in a humidity/moisture chamber, wipe away excess block with soft tissue (do not dry), apply 300 µL secondary antibody solution, gently cover with Parafilm®M, and incubate in a closed humidity/moisture chamber for 1 h at room temperature protected from light.

steps.title: Wash after secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash slides with PBS three times, 5 min each.

steps.title: Prepare Hoechst nuclear stain
steps.instruction: Make Hoechst solution 1 : 1000 diluted in dH₂O, enough for 300 µL per slide; protect the solution from light.

steps.title: Stain nuclei with Hoechst
steps.instruction: Lay slides horizontally in a humidity/moisture chamber, wipe away excess PBS with soft tissue (do not dry), apply 300 µL Hoechst solution to each slide for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Final PBS wash
steps.instruction: Wash slides with PBS three times, 5 min each.

steps.title: Mount with anti‑fade medium
steps.instruction: For each slide, wipe off excess PBS and mount a glass coverslip using 150 µL anti‑fade Floromount‑Go® (SouthernBiotech 0100‑01, L3220‑ZD30) mounting medium.

steps.title: Dry slides in darkness
steps.instruction: Leave slides to dry on a slide tray, covered with aluminium foil (complete darkness).

steps.title: Digitally scan and label slides
steps.instruction: Digitally scan slides soon after staining, label each slide with a pencil, and place them into a slide rack.

steps.title: Verify negative and positive controls
steps.instruction: Ensure the negative control shows no signal and the positive control shows the expected signal.
